newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends mixed in range dealing.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends mixed in range dealing.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL

PALM OIL FUTURES - Prices closed mixed after drifted in tight ranges as keen participation was absent. Activity was confined to spread trades. The market expect to be easier in short-term on expectation of poor export business. Trading was cautious and April futures trade between 1,268 and 1,276.
PALM OIL PHYSICAL - Also traded in line with futures and interest was seen among Feb CPOs and selected products.
Trading was cautious with players unwilling to take up huge positions ahead of the release of the January export data later this week by cargo surveyor (SGS) Sdn Bhd.
"We don't expect a good export for January. People are estimating at around 500,000 tonnes for this month," the trader added.

"The market is seen a bit bearish in the short-term due to lack of fresh demand," the trader said. "Buyers are likely to stay away from the market because palm oil is still highly priced compared with other vegetable oils."
But some recoveries would be seen in the long-term as the market felt of a lower production in February which will be a short working month.
Third month, April futures closed unchanged at its overnight closing level of 1,274 ringgit ($510.21) per tonne
Physical Feb (south) crude palm oil was offered at 1,335 against bids at 1,330 after trading at 1,325 to 1,330.
Feb (central) was offered at 1,335 and bids at 1,330 with early trades at 1,330 and Feb (north) at 1,317.50 against 1,312.50.
